episode_title: How Lenses Are Made with Zack Wildman from LensFactory

real_qa.q: What is Lens Factory's business model and how does it differ from traditional optometrists?
real_qa.r: Lens Factory focuses on selling new lenses while customers keep their existing frames, rather than trying to sell complete new glasses. This is a niche service because when customers get a new prescription at traditional optometrists, those optometrists try to sell them entirely new frames. Lens Factory makes seven or eight thousand pairs of glasses a day and wants to help people see effectively by putting new lenses in frames they've already been styled for.
real_qa.requete: Lens Factory keep frames replace lenses

real_qa.q: What are the main types of optical lenses and how do progressive lenses differ from bifocals?
real_qa.r: Single vision lenses let you see at one distance—either close, intermediate like a computer, or far away. Bifocals have a small section at the bottom for close vision and the top for distance. Trifocals add a middle distance range. Progressive lenses are no-line bifocals or trifocals that give all three distance ranges depending on where you look in the lens, and digital progressive lenses provide an even larger field of vision compared to traditional bifocals where you have to move your head.
real_qa.requete: progressive lenses vs bifocals trifocals difference

real_qa.q: How many employees does Lens Factory have and where are their offices located?
real_qa.r: Lens Factory employs 650 people today. They have an office and full lab set up in Louisville, as well as an additional office and lab in Fort Lauderdale.
real_qa.requete: Lens Factory employees offices Louisville Fort Lauderdale

real_qa.q: What is Lens Factory's approach to customer service compared to AI chatbots?
real_qa.r: Lens Factory prioritizes having actual people answer calls and emails rather than relying on AI chatbots. While chatbots are useful for simple queries like order status, Lens Factory believes that for vision-related questions, customers need human support because people may not have the same understanding or knowledge about what they need. The company stresses that you can have great customer service with a mediocre product and customers will return, but a high-end product with horrible customer service won't bring customers back.
real_qa.requete: Lens Factory customer service human support vs chatbots

real_qa.q: When did Lens Factory launch and how was it acquired?
real_qa.r: Lens Factory was acquired by PDS Optical in mid-2021 as a brand. Before the acquisition, Lens Factory's employees worked in the same building as PDS Optical and were already fulfilling orders. After deciding not to continue with their new glasses brand that launched on March 27, 2020, Wildman proposed acquiring Lens Factory to the PDS Optical owners.
